::: {.callout-warning title="Preliminary diagnostic output"}
This report describes classifier-selected births. It does not establish that those
births had Down syndrome or recover the full missed-case population.
:::

The plots compare three cohorts:

- **Recorded** births have `down_ind = 1`.
- **Classifier-selected** births carry the configured `ds_pred_missing*` flag.
  They are high-scoring unrecorded births selected within year and month.
- **Combined** births are the union of those cohorts.

The default quota is `ceil(1.5 × recorded)` selected births per year and month.
It fixes the selected count relative to the recorded count. It does not estimate
the number of missed diagnoses. Use the saved run metadata to identify the score
and flag columns; model variants can use different training labels.

A classifier trained on the recorded flag predicts that flag. The score is not a
validated probability of true Down syndrome among unrecorded births. Differences
in cohort shares show how selection changes the composition. They do not directly
measure recording sensitivity or prove that under-reporting has been corrected.

The analysis script copies this template into the run directory with its tables
and figures. Each grouping uses the rows available for its variables, so check
its denominator before comparing shares across sections.

```{python}
# | echo: false
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
from dspopulations_us_birth_certificates.report_readers import read_csv_artefact, read_json_artefact
from IPython.display import Markdown

config = read_json_artefact(Path("config.json"))


def _load_summary(variable: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return read_csv_artefact(f"{variable}_summary.csv")


def _render_summary_table(summary: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    count_cols = ["predicted_n", "recorded_n", "rprime_n"]
    pct_cols = ["predicted_pct", "recorded_pct", "rprime_pct"]
    display_df = summary[["label", *count_cols, *pct_cols]].copy()
    for c in count_cols:
        display_df[c] = display_df[c].map(lambda v: f"{int(v):,}")
    for c in pct_cols:
        display_df[c] = display_df[c].map(lambda v: f"{float(v):.2f}")
    display_df = display_df.rename(
        columns={
            "label": "Category",
            "predicted_n": "Classifier-selected (n)",
            "predicted_pct": "Classifier-selected (%)",
            "recorded_n": "Recorded (n)",
            "recorded_pct": "Recorded (%)",
            "rprime_n": "Combined (n)",
            "rprime_pct": "Combined (%)",
        }
    )
    return display_df.set_index("Category")
```

```{python}

    year_range = f"{config['start_year']}–{config['end_year']}"
flag_column = config.get("flag_column", "ds_pred_missing")
predictions_column = config.get("predictions_column", "p_ds_lb_pred_01")
restrict = config.get("restrict_to_prediction_coverage", True)
scope = (
    f"rows with non-null `{predictions_column}` (i.e. within the "
    "prediction model's coverage)"
    if restrict
    else "all rows, regardless of prediction coverage"
)

# Headline totals come from mracehisp (all three groupings see the same
# population of rows, so any one can stand in).
headline = _load_summary("mracehisp").iloc[-1]

Markdown(
    f"- **DuckDB**: `{config['duckdb_path']}`\n"
    f"- **classifier-selection flag**: `{flag_column}`\n"
    f"- **predictions column**: `{predictions_column}`\n"
    f"- **year range**: {year_range}\n"
    f"- **scope**: {scope}\n"
    f"- **recorded total**: {int(headline['recorded_n']):,}\n"
    f"- **classifier-selected total**: {int(headline['predicted_n']):,}\n"
    f"- **recorded + classifier-selected total**: {int(headline['rprime_n']):,}"
)
```

## Evidence and interpretation

The [Atlanta validation study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3056031/)
found low certificate sensitivity and variation with maternal, infant and hospital
characteristics across selected defects. Its pooled associations must not all be
read as Down syndrome-specific estimates or as national rates.

The [positive-unlabelled learning survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.04820)
explains why labelled positives and an unlabelled mixture need additional
assumptions to infer true status. This project also allows false-positive flags,
so the recorded positives are not assumed to be a perfect diagnostic reference.

Feature removal can change which births rank highly. Agreement with a literature
pattern does not validate selected births as missed cases. Co-occurring-condition
shares and demographic distributions in the combined cohort remain selection-dependent.

## Maternal age (`mage_c`)

Banded into eight groups: under 20, 20–24, 25–29, 30–34, 35–39, 40–44,
45–49, and 50+. Totals per group are computed over the report's
configured year range, which defaults to 2016–2024.

![Recorded vs. classifier-selected births by maternal age](mage_c_recorded_vs_predicted.png){#fig-mage-c .lightbox fig-align="center"}

```{python}
# | echo: false
_render_summary_table(_load_summary("mage_c"))
```

## Maternal race / Hispanic origin (`mracehisp`)

`mracehisp` is the NCHS combined race/Hispanic-origin recode for the
mother. The integer codes here follow the 2014-revision scheme
(1 = NH White only, 2 = NH Black only, 3 = NH AIAN only, 4 = NH Asian
only, 5 = NH NHOPI only, 6 = NH more than one race, 7 = Hispanic,
8 = Origin unknown or not stated). The raw column has different codes before 2014. These labels are intended
for the default 2016–2024 window. An earlier-year report needs compatible
codes and coverage. See the
[race audit](https://github.com/dspopulations/us-birth-certificates/blob/main/notes/202604201112-mracehisp-error.md).

![Recorded vs. classifier-selected births by maternal race/Hispanic origin](mracehisp_recorded_vs_predicted.png){#fig-mracehisp .lightbox fig-align="center"}

```{python}
# | echo: false
_render_summary_table(_load_summary("mracehisp"))
```

## Maternal education (`meduc`)

`meduc` takes nine values, from `8th grade or less` through to
`Doctorate or professional degree`, with a final `Unknown` code. Rows
with a NULL `meduc` are excluded (large numbers of pre-2003 records
and some later state-level gaps).

## Birth weight (`dbwt`)

Birth weight in grams, banded into clinical buckets. The lowest band
`Under 1500 g` corresponds to the VLBW (very-low-birth-weight)
threshold; the second band covers the rest of the LBW range. A `Not
stated` bucket (the NCHS `dbwt = 9999` sentinel) is retained so the
report shows how much of the denominator has an unknown weight.

![Recorded vs. classifier-selected births by birth weight](dbwt_recorded_vs_predicted.png){#fig-dbwt .lightbox fig-align="center"}

```{python}
# | echo: false
_render_summary_table(_load_summary("dbwt"))
```

## Gestational age at delivery (`gestrec10`)

NCHS's ten-level gestational-age recode plus an `Unknown` bucket

weeks), late-term (41 weeks) and post-term (≥ 42 weeks) categories.

## Checks before interpretation

Check the model's training years, label definition, prediction coverage and quota.
Compare feature sets on the same cohort and denominators. Assess recorded-label
performance on data not used for tuning where possible. Validation of true missed
cases would need an independent diagnosis source.

The current extract has no state or hospital identifier. A proposed state or
hospital analysis cannot be produced from these rows. Differences between quota
specifications form a sensitivity comparison, not a credible interval.
